note: Locations are approximate (for orientation, not navigation). Every row carries a public source. Stages: operating | approved | development | advanced | exploration | legacy.

mines.name: Red Chris
mines.detail: Open pit since 2015. Block-cave transition approved through the Tahltan consent-based process in June 2026; on the federal Major Projects Office first tranche; ~$500M in federal support announced July 2026. Extends mine life to the mid-2040s.

mines.name: Brucejack
mines.detail: High-grade underground gold mine, in production since 2017.

mines.name: Dome Mountain
mines.detail: Small underground operation (~100–150 t/day) that reached commercial production in May 2026.

mines.name: Eskay Creek (restart)
mines.detail: The first mine approved under a Declaration Act Section 7 consent agreement with the Tahltan Nation: EA certificate, Mines Act permit and federal approvals, January 2026.

mines.name: KSM (Kerr-Sulphurets-Mitchell)
mines.detail: One of the world's largest undeveloped gold-copper projects (47.3 Moz gold, 7.3 Blb copper in reserves; US$1.2B spent). In June 2026 the BC Supreme Court upheld its 'substantially started' designation as reasonable but ordered a 90-day consultation with the Tsetsaut Skii km Lax Ha Nation and EAO reconsideration.

mines.name: Galore Creek
mines.detail: Large copper-gold project; BC and the Tahltan opened consent-agreement discussions on its review in 2023. Teck cites ~1,200 direct jobs at build-out.

mines.name: Schaft Creek
mines.detail: One of Canada's largest undeveloped copper porphyries, at scoping stage.

mines.name: Turnagain
mines.detail: Large nickel-cobalt project in Kaska country; 2023 PFS outlines ~2.17 Blb of nickel over roughly 30 years.

mines.name: Kutcho
mines.detail: Feasibility-stage copper-zinc project ~100 km east of Dease Lake, in the federal EA process; drilling in July 2026.

mines.name: Cassiar Gold
mines.detail: Exploration-stage gold project at the historic Cassiar district.

mines.name: Premier / Cambria (Ascot)
mines.stage_label: Restarted 2024, operations suspended — status to confirm
mines.detail: Historic Premier mine restarted in 2024, then suspended operations. Current status marked for team verification before launch.

mines.name: Tulsequah Chief
mines.owner: Abandoned (remediation: BC · Taku River Tlingit · Teck)
mines.stage_label: Closed — leaking acid drainage for ~65 years
mines.detail: Abandoned in 1957 and leaking acid rock drainage into the Taku watershed ever since. A BC–Taku River Tlingit–Teck remediation framework (2024 MOU) targets a draft cleanup plan in 2026 and a final plan by 2028.
